title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench, a paired comparison of a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline on 1,200 intent→config episodes using gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator, and Mininet‑style emulation. Our preregistered binary episode success required (a) validator acceptance of the final configuration, (b) no emulator-observed availability degradation above tolerance, and (c) no automatic rollback. Of 1,200 planned paired tasks we completed 1,199 pairs: baseline success = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149); guarded success = 1,199/1,199 (1.0000000000). The paired‑success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025020851 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.0058381985], bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Per the peer review request, we explicitly disclose that the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) — a per‑cluster paired confirmatory breakdown — was not executed; only the pooled confirmatory analysis is archived (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json). Representative validator traces and provider audit logs show repair was invoked only three times. Given the observed near‑ceiling baseline, the preregistered power target (MDE = 5 pp) was not met for detecting much smaller absolute improvements; we report artifacts and analytic choices to support reproducible interpretation.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being integrated into NetOps workflows to translate operator intent into executable device configurations. Prior surveys and system proposals emphasize that operational reliability is a property of the orchestration stack—model plus deterministic validators, provenance, and sandboxed execution—rather than of the base LLM alone [see cited works]. Generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) architectures are a canonical mitigation pattern: an LLM proposes candidates, an automated verifier checks constraints and safety, and an automated repair loop iterates until acceptance. Despite conceptual support, preregistered, paired, emulator‑grounded evidence comparing verifier‑assisted pipelines to one‑shot generation on an operationally meaningful binary success metric (validator acceptance + no harmful emulator side effects + no rollback) is sparse. We address that gap with NetOpsTraceBench (study_id = rX4f7-1). The study asks: can a reproducible workflow‑centered benchmark of paired intent→config episodes produce an objective paired binary success metric that reliably distinguishes verifier‑assisted pipelines from one‑shot generation across two simulated topology clusters?
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers position LLMs as components inside broader AIOps/NetOps workflows and argue for workflow‑centered evaluation (trace quality, validator interactions, rollback‑aware metrics) rather than isolated one‑shot QA tests [references]. Concrete verifier‑assisted approaches appear in NL→formal translation and topology‑compilation work where verifiers drive iterative repairs; NetOps prototypes (text→config generators, misconfiguration detectors, LLM firewalls) implement variations of generate–validate‑repair and report feasibility on constructed evaluation sets [references]. Empirical analyses document LLM failure modes—hallucination, unit/semantic errors, miscalibration, provenance loss, and prompt‑injection risks—that motivate external verification and provenance linkers [references]. Collectively, this literature motivates a preregistered, artifact‑rich paired evaluation with deterministic seeds, explicit exclusion rules, and emulator ground truth to observe when and why verifier scaffolding alters operational outcomes.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: We preregistered NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1) and froze the experimental plan (preregistration SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) prior to model calls. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned confirmatory hypotheses included H1 (overall paired difference), H2 (failure‑mode catalogs), and H3 (paired confirmatory breakdown by topology cluster: edge vs core). Per the peer review request we now explicitly state that H3 was not executed; the archived analysis contains only the pooled confirmatory analysis artifacts listed below. The archived pooled artifacts used for the reported inferential results are: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, and execution/execution_manifest.json (all included in the published run artifacts). No per‑cluster confirmatory contingency tables were produced or archived for H3.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: The run completed 2,398 of 2,400 planned episodes and produced 1,199 complete paired observations. Provider audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1; stage_counts show shared_initial_generation = 1,200 and repair = 3. Primary pooled confirmatory counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are: n11 = 1,196, n10 = 3, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline_success_rate = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149; guarded_success_rate = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0000000000; paired difference = 0.0025020851. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 (archived in analysis/results.json). Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) for the paired difference is [0.0000, 0.0058381985] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg). Missingness summary: complete_pairs = 1,199; failed_baseline_episodes = 1; failed_guarded_episodes = 1; both_missing_pairs = 1 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Repair invocation: repair stage calls = 3 and repair_applied = true only on those three episodes; validator traces show validation_after.valid = true for the majority of episodes (execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: The pooled confirmatory analysis shows no statistically significant advantage for the guarded pipeline under the supplied corpus and validator configuration (p = 0.25; CI includes zero). Two artifact‑grounded explanations are supported by archived traces. First, baseline one‑shot generation exhibited near‑ceiling success (≈99.75%), leaving little absolute headroom; the preregistered MDE targeted 5 percentage points and thus the study was underpowered to detect much smaller gains. Second, deterministic task generation and validator settings produced many clear, strictly specified required sequences; the guarded pipeline therefore rarely required repair (repair = 3), limiting observable differences on a binary success metric. These interpretations are supported directly by task_manifest entries (declared difficulty levels and required_sequence arrays), scoring artifacts (validation_before/after), and provider audit logs (stage_counts).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired, emulator‑grounded comparison of one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→configuration pipelines on 1,199 complete pairs. Under the synthetic task corpus, deterministic validator settings, and gpt-5-mini as requested, baseline generation achieved near‑ceiling success and the guarded pipeline produced a small absolute increase (≈0.25 percentage points) that was not statistically significant (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% bootstrap CI includes zero). Crucially, the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) was not executed; only the pooled confirmatory analysis is archived (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json). The run artifacts and logs provide a reproducible basis for follow‑up sensitivity studies that vary task adversariality, verifier strictness, and model families to determine conditions under which verifier scaffolding yields operationally meaningful improvements.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (preregistered run rX4f7-1). LLM(s) and provider: requested_model = gpt-5-mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json (requested_model=gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens=1500) is archived. Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed the paired benchmark. Deterministic tooling: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed canonical parsing and intent‑constraint validation; deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced synthetic tasks. Exact initial master prompt: provenance/master_prompt.txt (immutable reference SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration: NetOpsTraceBench (ID rX4f7-1) preregistration manifest SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712; confirmatory hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion rules, seeds, stopping rules, and analysis plan were frozen before execution. Execution summary and key archived artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (completed pairs = 1,199; model_calls_used = 1,203; repair_stage_calls = 3), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, and analysis/missingness_summary.csv. Important disclosure about preregistered H3: the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3: per‑cluster paired confirmatory breakdown) was not executed; only the pooled confirmatory analysis artifacts listed above were produced and archived. Analytic deviation: the preregistration specified a nonparametric paired test; because outcomes were binary the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar two‑sided test plus a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000); this deviation is documented in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Reproducibility: raw model outputs, provider traces, validator traces, task_manifest, transformation_manifest, execution logs, and analysis code plus all seeds are archived (artifact_count = 8,408; full manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Human involvement: the Research Director selected the topic family and approved the master prompt pre‑lock; after autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature review, preregistration drafting, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review response, and revision. Technical restarts and deviations: execution manifest records two failed episodes and the analytic deviation described above; all deviations are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl. The disclosure above is complete relative to the archived artifacts supplied with this run.
limitations: Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, and other deployment failure modes.

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary (documented in analysis/results.json).

Preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) was not executed; only the pooled confirmatory analysis is archived (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json).
